You broke the dream of my life.
What kind of report will he write now?
Viktor Petrovich, maybe it will blow over?

Why did you do that just now?

And right now he will not create any?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'ask for', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Я тебя в прошлый раз просил.
examples.trans: I asked you last time.
Please do everything that he asks.
I apologise.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Just do not worry.
You will not withstand a blow from a coconut.
I will not withstand such a blow?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: After you, it is very close by.
Quickly hold him right here!
Everyone here wants to kill me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').

examples.trans: Well, I am completely alive.
After you, it is very close by.
Chef, this is somehow completely insecure.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'далеко'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: After you, it is very close by.
The apple does not fall far from the tree.
We live not far from the center.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ломать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'broke', paired with 'ломать'.

examples.trans: You broke the dream of my life.
Two fingers are broken.
Who broke the door?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'dream, wish' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You broke the dream of my life.
Those are silly childish dreams.
That is my dream.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello, did my husband stop by here?
After all, I live with my mother.
Denis, thank you, you are my savior!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You broke the dream of my life.
This is your life's work, after all.
That's life.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('what').

examples.trans: What kind of report will he write now?
How foolish you are!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'report, account' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: What kind of report will he write now?
He returned with a report.

examples.text: Шеф, наш разведчик вернулся с отчётом.
examples.trans: Chef, our scout has returned with a report.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It overshadowed that unpleasant incident.
Of course, you are completely free.
What kind of report will he write now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: You must not be overfed right now.
Maybe tomorrow, or maybe right now.
Let us test it right now!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'писать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will write', paired with 'писать'.

examples.trans: I suggest writing a good review.
He wrote a statement.
Write to me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'maybe', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You can throw a coconut at me.
Maybe tomorrow, or maybe right now.
Viktor Petrovich, maybe it will blow over?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Is everything alright with you?
We will wash everything out quickly.
We will fix everything!

meanings.en: to get by without, manage without
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ойтись'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will do', paired with 'обходиться'.

examples.trans: Try to manage without our help.
We will easily manage without a car.

examples.text: Постарайтесь обойтись без нашей помощи. — Спасибо вам огромное!
examples.trans: Try to manage without our help. — Thank you so much!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We will wash everything out quickly.
We will fix everything!
We do not wish you any harm.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then, afterwards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I will explain everything later.
We will feed him deliciously later.
Later they will put me on the wanted list.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We will feed him deliciously later.
It's delicious!
Mum is a good cook.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'кормить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will feed'.

examples.trans: We will feed him deliciously later.
The cook fed the guests deliciously.

examples.text: Раз не можем напоить, мы его накормим!
examples.trans: Since we cannot give him drink, we will feed him!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'звать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'name', paired with 'называть'.

examples.trans: You called me a bad word.
What will you name your son?

examples.text: Ты назвал меня плохим словом. Меня, начальника!
examples.trans: You called me a bad word. Me, your boss!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.
You must not be overfed right now.
I am inspecting your restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'at least', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Хотите пойти к себе в номер?
examples.trans: Do you want to go to your room?
Name me at least one reason.
He wanted to speak with the chef.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Fedya, escort the man, please.
I locked him in the refrigerator.
Hello, did my husband stop by here?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'чина'). Common feminine noun meaning 'an excuse, a reason' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Name me at least one reason.

examples.text: Нет причин держать вас под арестом.
examples.trans: There is no reason to keep you under arrest.
What is the reason?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'переть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'locked'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и запереть вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and locked on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют запереть.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to locked.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello, Viktor Petrovich.
I am inspecting your restaurant.
Is everything alright with you?

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'fridge' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I locked him in the refrigerator.
The milk is in the fridge.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'why', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Then why did you hit me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You will not withstand a blow from a coconut.

How foolish you are!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It overshadowed that unpleasant incident.
What kind of total nonsense is this?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'made', paired with 'делать'.

examples.trans: Why did you do that just now?
I did just that yesterday.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'but, after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: A coconut has already fallen on me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'ourselves', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You hinted at it to me yourself.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'мекать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to hint, imply'.

examples.trans: You hinted at it to me yourself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: If we let him go, he will create problems.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'пустить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to let go, to release', paired with 'отпускать'.

examples.trans: Let me go from here, please.
If we let him go, he will create problems.
Viktor Petrovich, please let us go.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оздать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to create, establish', paired with 'создавать'.

examples.trans: If we let him go, he will create problems.
And right now he will not create any?

examples.text: Мы создадим идеальную команду для работы.
examples.trans: We will create an ideal team for work.

meanings.note: Borrowed via Polish/German from Greek 'problema' (something thrown forward, a task or question).

examples.trans: If we let him go, he will create problems.
That's not a problem.
I have a problem.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'anything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Now we will think of something, Chef.

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

придумать.gloss: to think up, to come up with

meanings.en: to think up, to invent, to come up with
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'думать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think up, to come up with', paired with 'придумывать'.

examples.trans: Now we will think of something, Chef.
You came up with this yourself!
I'll think up a plan.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('foolish').

examples.trans: This is just a foolish misunderstanding.
